# ADR-001: Build a small bespoke orchestration core on audited libraries

- Status: Proposed (pending Codex challenge and user approval)
- Date: 2026-10-22

## Context
The user asked whether ATLAS should adopt an existing open-source orchestrator instead of building one. They added that the result "must be secured well". ATLAS's distinguishing requirements are:
- gated adversarial review with an evidence model;
- independence enforcement;
- idempotent, reconciled GitHub side effects;
- durable crash recovery;
- subscription-only, terms-respecting agent use (including manual Antigravity);
- strict prompt-injection boundaries.

## Options evaluated (desk research, 2026-10-22)

| Option | What it is | Fit | Security / trust concerns |
|---|---|---|---|
| Vibe Kanban, claude-squad, Conductor, Emdash, Rove | UIs/TUIs to run several coding agents side by side in worktrees | Covers worktree management only. No plan challenge, evidence-gated merges, outbox, or policy engine | Fast-moving; no published security audits found. Usually runs agents in permissive modes. Would hold gh credentials for every repo |
| Orchestrator.inc `agent-orchestrator` (Apache-2.0) | Desktop + mobile app for agent teams, task to merged PR | Closest in scope | Large surface (desktop + mobile + remote). Unclear credential handling and remote components. Adopting it means trusting the vendor's code path to merge into main |
| claw-orchestrator | Headless runtime for multiple CLIs incl. Antigravity; "done only when checks it didn't write pass" | Good ideas (independent checks) | Automates Antigravity, which conflicts with ADR-003. Spend-cap features are aimed at API billing |
| Temporal / Prefect / Hatchet | Durable workflow engines | Durable execution | Need a server and Postgres. Violates the "no unnecessary infra" constraint |
| DBOS Transact (MIT) | Library-level durable workflows | Attractive model | Python version is Postgres-first. SQLite support for Python not confirmed. Adds a framework whose semantics we must trust for recovery |
| LangGraph (+ SQLite checkpointer) | Agent graph framework | Checkpointing | Designed around direct LLM API calls, not CLI subprocesses. Heavy dependency for little gain |

Sources: [augmentcode survey](https://www.augmentcode.com/tools/open-source-agent-orchestrators), [OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator), [claw-orchestrator](https://github.com/Enderfga/claw-orchestrator), [DBOS Python](https://github.com/DBOS-project/dbos-transact-py), [DBOS June 2026 update](https://dbos.dev/blog/new-in-dbos-june-2026).

## Decision
**Build** a small core for the security-critical parts:
- FSM + transition log;
- policy engine (gates, independence, diff guards);
- outbox + reconciliation;
- supervisor;
- adapters;
- handoff validation.

Estimated size: roughly 3–5k lines of Python, each piece unit-testable in isolation.

**Adopt** well-known, widely deployed libraries and tools for everything else:
- FastAPI, Pydantic, SQLAlchemy/Alembic, SQLite, structlog;
- React, Vite, Tailwind;
- pytest, Hypothesis, Vitest, Playwright;
- the official provider CLIs, git, gh.

## Consequences
- **Plus:** full control over the parts where bugs lead to bad merges or terms violations. A minimal dependency surface, and no third-party code holding credentials.
- **Minus:** we write and maintain the recovery logic ourselves. This is mitigated by the crash-point fault-injection suite (recovery-strategy.md §5).
- **Reopen if:** a mature library emerges with SQLite-native durable workflows for Python, or the user prefers a specific tool after their own review.

## Supply-chain controls
- Locked dependencies with hashes.
- `pip-audit` / `npm audit` in CI.
- Renovate/Dependabot.
- Licence check: MIT/BSD/Apache only.
- Each new runtime dependency is justified in its PR.
# ADR-002: SQLite WAL + transactional outbox instead of a workflow engine

- Status: Proposed
- Date: 2026-10-22

## Context
ATLAS must survive crashes and restarts and must never duplicate external side effects. It runs on one Mac for one user, at low volume.

## Decision
- Persist all workflow state in SQLite (WAL, `synchronous=FULL`) through a single writer.
- Model every external side effect as an `outbox_ops` row (intent → execute → confirm) with an idempotency key.
- On restart, reconcile against ground truth (git, `gh`) before retrying.
- The FSM records only confirmed facts.

## Alternatives
- **Temporal, Prefect, Hatchet:** these need extra servers.
- **DBOS:** Postgres-first in Python.
- **Pure event sourcing:** more machinery than needed. The append-only `transitions` table already gives an audit history.

## Consequences
- One file to back up, and nothing extra to operate.
- Reconciliation logic is custom per operation. That is a small, enumerable set, and each operation has a fault-injection test.
- Horizontal scaling is not possible. That's acceptable; it's a non-goal.
# ADR-003: Google Antigravity is integrated via user-run manual handoff only

- Status: Accepted by user on 2026-10-22, pending Codex challenge
- Date: 2026-10-22

## Context
- The [Antigravity terms](https://antigravity.google/terms) §6 say users must not use the Service "in connection with products not provided by us". They also call "using third party software, tools, or services to access the Service" a breach, which can lead to suspension.
- The [Headless docs](https://antigravity.google/docs/cli/headless/) document `agy -p` for scripting and CI. Google has not stated that a *third-party local orchestrator* may invoke it on a consumer AI Pro account. Forum replies saying it is fine come from unverified community members.
- The forum shows users reporting 403 ToS suspensions after using third-party tools.
- `agy` print mode has open bugs: a non-TTY hang (#318) and `permissions.allow` being ignored in print mode (#548).

## Decision
- ATLAS never spawns `agy`, never automates the Antigravity IDE, and never touches Antigravity credentials.
- Antigravity steps produce a handoff packet. The user runs Antigravity personally and imports a schema-validated `result.json`. See [antigravity-manual-handoff.md](../antigravity-manual-handoff.md).
- Imported results carry the evidence label `manual_imported`. They never count as `executed`.

## Consequences
- QA through Antigravity needs the user to be present. The Definition of Done reports this limitation explicitly.
- Fallback (opt-in, per task): reassign QA to the headless agent that did not implement the phase. The UI shows that Antigravity was not used.
- **Revisit when** Google publishes explicit permission for local programmatic invocation on consumer plans. Any future headless adapter will be a separately challenged phase.
# ADR-004: Agents are invoked only as unmodified official CLIs via subprocess

- Status: Proposed
- Date: 2026-10-22

## Decision
- Claude Code and Codex are run as their unmodified binaries (`claude -p …`, `codex exec …`), as the logged-in macOS user, with subscription login managed solely by those CLIs.
- ATLAS never reads, copies, stores or proxies provider tokens. It never uses the Agent SDK with subscription credentials, never runs browser automation and never calls provider HTTP endpoints directly.
- `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `OPENAI_API_KEY` and `CODEX_API_KEY` are stripped from agent environments, so billing cannot silently switch to an API account.
- ATLAS is a personal tool. It must not be offered as a hosted or multi-user service that uses anyone else's subscription. [Claude terms](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/legal-and-compliance) forbid routing requests through Pro/Max credentials "on behalf of their users".
- Codex on **public** repositories is blocked by default. [OpenAI docs](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/non-interactive-mode) say: "Do not use this workflow for public or open-source repositories."

## Consequences
- Startup capability probes and version pinning cover CLI flag drift.
- Exact quota numbers are unavailable. The capacity state is inferred from documented signals only.
# ADR-005: Review independence is enforced by provider *and* model family

- Status: Proposed
- Date: 2026-10-22

## Context
Antigravity can run Claude and GPT-OSS models (`evidence/agy-models.txt`). Claude Code and Codex may also expose models from several families over time. If the reviewer and the author share a model family, they tend to share the same blind spots.

## Decision
- Every artifact (plan, phase diff, fix) records `author_agent` and `author_model`.
- A reviewer, challenger or QA agent is assigned only if `provider ≠ author provider` **and** `model_family(reviewer_model) ≠ model_family(author_model)`.
- Model family mapping:
  - `claude-*` → anthropic;
  - `gpt-*`, `o*` and Codex defaults → openai;
  - `gemini-*` → google;
  - unknown → `unknown`, which counts as matching the author's family, so independence is not satisfied.
- If independence cannot be met, the step goes to `AWAITING_MANUAL` or `BLOCKED`. The author is never used as the sole reviewer.
- A fix to a finding is "verified" only by an independent reviewer's re-check on the new SHA, plus re-executed tests.

## Consequences
- With the default roles, the developer is Codex (openai), the code reviewer is Claude (anthropic), and QA is Antigravity on a Gemini model (google). That gives three distinct families.
- Losing one provider may block mandatory reviews. This is intentional, because the brief requires that independence never be sacrificed.

# ATLAS Architecture

Status: Phase 0 draft · Date: 2026-10-22 · Owner: Lead architect (Claude Code), challenger: Codex

## 1. Goals and non-goals

**Goals**
- Turn a high-level software request into a phased, dependency-ordered plan. Execute it one phase at a time, through gated stages: plan, challenge, implement, test, review, QA, commit, PR, merge, checkpoint.
- Use only official, subscription-authenticated agent interfaces. Never touch provider credentials.
- Survive crashes, restarts and quota exhaustion without duplicating external side effects.
- Isolate projects from each other: repo, config, queue, state, worktrees, agent context.
- Never report an action that did not happen.

**Non-goals (first release)**
- Hosting ATLAS for other people. ATLAS is a single-user local tool; see ADR-004.
- Running several code-changing phases in one repository at the same time.
- Production deployment. ATLAS stops at "merged + verified CI". Deployment verification is a pluggable, opt-in hook.
- Automating Google Antigravity (ADR-003).

## 2. Context diagram

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  user([User]) -->|browser, localhost only| ui[Dashboard\nReact + Vite]
  user -->|manual handoff| agyUser[Antigravity IDE / agy\nrun BY THE USER]
  ui -->|REST + SSE| api[ATLAS Core\nFastAPI process]
  api --> db[(SQLite WAL\n~/.atlas/atlas.db)]
  api --> fs[(Artifact store\n~/.atlas/artifacts)]

ATLAS never runs `agy`. The user does, and imports the result (see [antigravity-manual-handoff.md](antigravity-manual-handoff.md)).

## 3. Process model

A single Python 3.12 process (`atlas serve`) contains:

| Component | Responsibility |
|---|---|
| **API layer** (FastAPI) | REST endpoints and SSE event stream for the dashboard. Binds to `127.0.0.1` only and requires a per-install session token. |
| **Orchestrator** | The only component allowed to change workflow state. Applies validated FSM transitions inside DB transactions. Reads gate policy from config, never from agent output. |
| **Scheduler** | Chooses the next runnable phase across projects: priority, dependency satisfaction, repo lock, agent capacity. Default concurrency is one code-changing phase per repo and one global agent invocation per provider. |
| **Supervisor** | asyncio task that spawns and monitors subprocesses: agents, git, gh, test commands. Records PID, process start time, process group, and stdout/stderr artifact files. Enforces timeouts and sends SIGINT → SIGTERM → SIGKILL in that order. |
| **Agent adapters** | One per provider. Build an argv from a vetted template, parse output into typed results, and classify failures into capacity states. Never interpret agent text as instructions to ATLAS. |
| **Capacity manager** | Tracks per-provider state (AVAILABLE, BUSY, RATE_LIMITED, QUOTA_EXHAUSTED, AUTHENTICATION_REQUIRED, PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE, UNKNOWN, MANUAL_ONLY). Runs bounded backoff and cheap auth probes. |
| **Repository service** | Clone, fetch, worktree add/remove, branch, diff, commit, reconciliation. Wraps git only; it is not an agent. |
| **GitHub service** | Wraps `gh` for PR, checks, reviews and merge. Every mutating call goes through the outbox (see [recovery-strategy.md](recovery-strategy.md)). |
| **Test runner** | Runs project-configured test commands at the candidate commit, **inside the enforced test sandbox** (security-model.md §5.1; fails closed if unavailable), and captures structured results. These are the *executed* results, distinct from what an agent reports. |
| **Policy engine** | Pure functions. Given the config, the phase and the evidence, it answers questions such as "may we merge?" and "is the reviewer independent?". Fully unit-tested. |
| **Handoff service** | Creates and validates manual-handoff packets: Antigravity, and any step where an agent is unavailable. |
| **Recovery service** | Runs at startup before the scheduler. Reconciles DB state against git, GitHub and processes. |
| **Audit/log** | Structured JSON logs with correlation IDs, an append-only `transitions` table and `audit_log` table, and secret redaction. |

There is no Redis, broker or Postgres. A single process with SQLite is enough at this scale (ADR-002). `launchd` keeps it running (Phase 10).

```
~/.atlas/
  atlas.db                 # SQLite WAL (global + per-project rows, project_id FK everywhere)
  config.yaml              # global config (non-secret)
  projects/<project_id>/

Secrets are kept outside this tree. Phase 1+ stores ATLAS-managed secrets, such as an optional per-project fine-grained GitHub PAT, in the macOS Keychain under the service name `atlas.<project_id>.github`.

## 5. The delivery pipeline (per phase)

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A[Plan approved] --> B[Prepare worktree\nfrom latest base]
  B --> C[Implement\ndeveloper agent]
  C --> K[Candidate commit rN\ndiff guards, ATLAS-made]
  K --> D[Run tests in sandbox\nATLAS-executed on rN]
  D -->|fail| F[Repair loop\n≤ max_repair_attempts]
  F --> K
  D -->|pass| E[Code review\nindependent agent on rN diff]
  E -->|blocking findings| G[Fix → new candidate rN+1\nold evidence stale]
  G --> K
  E -->|clear| Q[QA on rN\nindependent / manual handoff]
  Q -->|fail| G
  Q -->|pass| H[Push rN → PR\noutbox]
  H --> I[CI + required approvals\non rN head]
  I -->|green + authorised| M[Merge\n--match-head-commit rN]
  M --> V[Confirm merge + update base\ncheckpoint]
  V --> N[Next runnable phase]
```

All evidence is bound to an immutable **candidate commit**, never to uncommitted worktree state. See [workflow-state-machine.md §0](workflow-state-machine.md). Gates are enforced by the policy engine. Any gate that cannot be satisfied because of missing evidence, capacity or a manual step moves the phase to `BLOCKED`, `AWAITING_MANUAL` or `AWAITING_APPROVAL`. The phase never moves forward without that evidence.

## 6. Evidence model

Every claim shown in the UI or in a report is labelled with its provenance:

| Label | Meaning | Example |
|---|---|---|
| `executed` | ATLAS ran it and captured exit code and output | `pytest` run by the test runner |
| `remote_verified` | ATLAS read it back from GitHub | PR merged, `mergeCommit` SHA |
| `agent_reported` | An agent said so (headless run, output parsed) | "I added tests for X" |
| `manual_imported` | Imported from a user-run handoff | Antigravity QA result |
| `proposed` | Suggested but not executed | "Run Playwright test Y" |

Gates accept only `executed` or `remote_verified` evidence for tests, CI and merge. Review and QA *findings* may be `agent_reported` or `manual_imported`. But a *fix* to a finding is accepted only when an independent reviewer re-checks it and the tests are re-executed.

## 7. Trust boundaries

1. **User ↔ ATLAS.** Trusted. Localhost UI with a token.
2. **ATLAS ↔ agent CLIs.** The CLI binaries are trusted as published. Their *output* is untrusted data. Agents run with cwd set to the phase worktree, with a scrubbed env (no `GH_TOKEN`, no ATLAS secrets) and restrictive permission flags.
3. **ATLAS ↔ repository content.** Untrusted. This includes READMEs, `AGENTS.md`/`CLAUDE.md`, `.claude/`, `.codex/`, `.mcp.json`, issues, CI logs and PR comments. ATLAS policy never comes from repo content (see [security-model.md](security-model.md)).
4. **ATLAS ↔ GitHub.** Authenticated through gh. Mutations are idempotent and reconciled.
5. **Project ↔ project.** Separate rows, worktrees, artifact references and handoff dirs. Agent invocations receive only the current project's worktree.

## 8. Configuration

Config is layered: built-in safe defaults → `~/.atlas/config.yaml` → `~/.atlas/projects/<id>/project.yaml` → per-task overrides (only fields marked overridable). A repository may *suggest* config, for example an `atlas.yaml` in the repo. ATLAS shows it as a proposal and applies it only after the user accepts it in the UI, because repo content is untrusted. Schema validation uses Pydantic, and unknown keys are rejected.

Safe defaults (must hold with an empty config):

```yaml
execution:  { mode: supervised, max_active_phases_per_repository: 1, max_review_cycles: 3, max_repair_attempts: 3 }
git:        { use_worktrees: true, create_pull_requests: true, auto_merge: false, merge_strategy: squash }
quality:    { require_tests: true, require_code_review: true, require_independent_qa: true,
              block_on_critical_findings: true, block_on_high_findings: true }
capacity:   { on_quota_exhausted: pause, allow_agent_substitution: false,
              allow_paid_api_fallback: false, allow_unsupported_integrations: false }
safety:     { allow_direct_main_changes: false, allow_force_push: false, allow_secret_modification: false,
              allow_destructive_database_commands: false, allow_production_deployment: false }

## 9. Agent role matrix and independence

The default role assignment follows the brief. The policy engine enforces **ADR-005**:
- The reviewer, challenger and QA agent for an artifact must differ from its author at both the *provider* level and the *model family* level.
- Example: Antigravity running a Claude model may not review Claude-authored work. The declared model is recorded at import.
- If independence cannot be satisfied with the available agents, the step goes to `AWAITING_MANUAL`. It is never silently fulfilled by the author.

| Role | Default | Allowed fallback (only if `allow_agent_substitution: true`) |
|---|---|---|
| architect / planner | claude | codex |
| plan challenger | codex | claude (only if plan author ≠ claude) |
| developer | codex | claude |
| code reviewer | claude | codex (only if developer ≠ codex) |
| QA | antigravity (manual) | the non-developer headless agent, with explicit per-task approval |

## 7. Timeouts, skipping and reassignment

- **Expiry:** a packet expires after `handoff.expiry_hours`, which defaults to 72 hours. Expired packets can be regenerated with one click. The new packet gets a new nonce.
- **Reminders:** the dashboard badge persists, and an optional daily notification is sent.
- **Skip:** QA can be skipped only if `quality.require_independent_qa` is `false` for the project. ATLAS writes a waiver to the audit log with your reason, and the final report lists the phase as **"QA waived by user"**.
- **Reassign:** with per-task approval, QA may go to the headless agent that is *not* the developer (for example Claude when Codex implemented). The UI states that Antigravity was not used.
- **If Antigravity finds problems** (`changes_required`): the phase returns to `FIXING`. After the fix, a **new** handoff packet is generated for re-verification. ATLAS does not accept the developer's claim that a finding is fixed.

    78	- Write roles (developer, fixer): preserve (§2.3), reset to the last candidate, then re-run. Optional (Phase 6): resume the provider session with the snapshot diff as context. Any output still becomes a *new candidate* and goes through the full gates.
    79	- A run counts as succeeded only when the exit code is 0, the final result was captured and parsed, and the process group is confirmed gone.
    80	
    81	## 3. Startup sequence (order matters)
    82	
    83	```
    84	1.  Open DB, PRAGMA quick_check → on failure: no scheduler; offer restore from latest backup
    85	2.  Acquire instance lock (flock on ~/.atlas/atlas.lock) → prevents two ATLAS processes
    86	3.  Discover executions (DB launching/running + ~/.atlas/run/*.json); QUIESCE all live groups (§2.2)
    87	4.  Probe agents (version/help hash/auth) → update agents table; nothing scheduled
    88	5.  For each project: git fetch (if network); `git worktree prune`; list worktrees vs phases
    89	6.  Repair interrupted git state in worktrees (only now that no writer is alive):
    90	       stale index.lock → remove; in-progress merge/rebase/cherry-pick → preserve (§2.3) then abort
    91	7.  Reconcile candidates: if a candidate commit exists on the branch but not in DB (crash after commit) → record it
    92	       by tree SHA; if DB has a candidate whose commit is missing → BLOCKED(candidate_missing)
    93	8.  Reconcile executions → interrupted; preserve worktrees with changes beyond the last candidate (§2.3)
    94	9.  Reconcile outbox ops (§1)
    95	10. Reconcile phases in PR_OPEN / CI_VALIDATION / MERGING / MERGE_PENDING_REMOTE against GitHub
    96	       (a human may have merged/closed; apply G-MERGED strictly)
    97	11. Release repo_locks held by dead instances only after their phase is PAUSED/BLOCKED/terminal
    98	12. Mark every in-progress phase PAUSED(resume_to=…) unless config `recovery.auto_resume: true`
    99	13. Audit "recovery_completed"; UI banner; start scheduler
   100	```
   101	
   102	The dashboard is read-only until step 13. Until Phase 6, `auto_resume` is forced to `false`: after any restart, everything waits for the user to press Resume (minimal safe restart, ATLAS-017).
   103	
   104	## 4. Capacity handling
   105	
   155	CREATE TABLE test_runs (
   156	  id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, project_id TEXT NOT NULL, phase_id TEXT NOT NULL, candidate_id TEXT NOT NULL,
   157	  execution_id TEXT, command TEXT NOT NULL, exit_code INTEGER, passed INTEGER, failed INTEGER, skipped INTEGER,

   159	  report_ref TEXT, created_at TEXT NOT NULL,

   161	  FOREIGN KEY (candidate_id, project_id) REFERENCES candidates(id, project_id),

   173	  criteria_json TEXT,                          -- QA: per-criterion status (validated complete; ATLAS-015)
   174	  execution_id TEXT, cycle INTEGER NOT NULL, created_at TEXT NOT NULL,

   183	  id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, project_id TEXT NOT NULL, review_round_id TEXT NOT NULL,

   185	  category TEXT NOT NULL, file TEXT, location TEXT, description TEXT NOT NULL,

   188	  fingerprint TEXT NOT NULL, created_at TEXT NOT NULL, updated_at TEXT NOT NULL,
   189	  UNIQUE (id, project_id),

   195	  justification TEXT NOT NULL, at_candidate_id TEXT, verified_by_round TEXT, approval_id TEXT,
   196	  created_at TEXT NOT NULL,
   197	  FOREIGN KEY (finding_id, project_id) REFERENCES findings(id, project_id),

  "verdict": "changes_required",
  "summary": "Reviewed all 18 round-1 findings against the revised documents. ATLAS-001, ATLAS-003, ATLAS-004 and ATLAS-014 remain incompletely resolved. The revisions also introduce four defects involving QA evidence, protected-path approvals, rebase recovery and rollback.",
  "findings": [
    {
      "id": "ATLAS-001",
      "severity": "CRITICAL",
      "category": "evidence-integrity",
      "file": "docs/security-model.md",
      "location": "§5.1, lines 113–114; docs/workflow-state-machine.md §3.1, G-TEST and G-MERGE-PRE",
      "description": "Candidate commits do not yet guarantee that tests execute the candidate content. Tests can modify tracked source in their writable worktree, and no required post-test integrity check invalidates evidence after those mutations.",
      "evidence": "The sandbox explicitly permits writes to the worktree. G-TEST requires an executed test_run with exit 0 and the current candidate_id, without checking that the tested source remained identical to the candidate. The documented cleanliness checks concern agent executions and candidate creation. A test can modify source, pass against that modification, and leave passing evidence attached to the different commit that is pushed.",
      "recommendation": "Execute tests against an enforced immutable source snapshot with separate writable output locations, or verify candidate identity and complete source integrity before and after every test execution and reject evidence on mutation."
    },
    {
      "id": "ATLAS-003",
      "severity": "CRITICAL",
      "category": "recovery-data-loss",
      "file": "docs/recovery-strategy.md",
      "location": "§2.3, lines 63–74",
      "description": "The snapshot preserves working-tree content but loses independently staged content before reset.",
      "evidence": "The temporary index is populated using add -A from the working tree. If a file contains version A in the real index and version B in the working tree, only B enters the snapshot. Verification compares working-tree content, so it can pass, after which reset destroys the only indexed reference to A. No copy of the original index or its staged tree is retained.",
      "recommendation": "Preserve the original index, staged blobs and conflict stages separately from the working-tree snapshot. Verify that both staged and working-tree states can be restored before allowing reset."
    },
    {
      "id": "ATLAS-004",
      "severity": "HIGH",
      "category": "process-recovery",
      "file": "docs/recovery-strategy.md",
      "location": "§2.1, lines 46–51; §3, lines 86–90; §5 launch crash-point row",
      "description": "The launch handshake still permits an undiscoverable child to start writing after recovery has completed process discovery.",
      "evidence": "The parent spawns atlas-exec before the child publishes its run file. If the parent crashes and the child is delayed before publication, startup sees a launching row with no PID and no run file. Nothing requires that launcher to wait for acknowledgement from the current supervisor before exec. It can later publish its file and execute the target while recovery repairs the worktree. The crash matrix incorrectly asserts that no orphan is possible in this interval.",
      "recommendation": "Require a supervisor acknowledgement before target exec, with a parent-liveness or generation check that prevents an unacknowledged launcher from proceeding after supervisor death. Recovery must settle every launching row before git repair."
    },
    {
      "id": "ATLAS-014",
      "severity": "HIGH",
      "category": "database-integrity",
      "file": "docs/database-design.md",
      "location": "§3, test_runs lines 155–163, review_rounds lines 166–179, handoffs lines 212–218; §4",
      "description": "Composite project foreign keys improve isolation but still do not enforce the subject relationships on which evidence gates depend, and several execution references remain unconstrained.",
      "evidence": "A test_run can reference phase A, candidate B and execution C from different phases of the same project; all declared foreign keys pass. review_rounds.execution_id and handoffs.execution_id have no execution foreign key at all. Likewise, a phase's task and plan can belong to different tasks within one project. The application integrity rules do not define validation of these relationships.",
      "recommendation": "Enforce candidate-to-phase, execution-to-candidate/phase and plan-to-task consistency through composite constraints or explicit transactional validators. Add missing execution foreign keys and negative tests for missing subjects and same-project mismatches."
    },
    {
      "id": "ATLAS-101",
      "severity": "HIGH",
      "category": "qa-evidence-integrity",
      "file": "docs/antigravity-manual-handoff.md",
      "location": "§2, line 61; §4, lines 107–108",
      "description": "The revised QA import policy explicitly accepts results obtained from modified source while assigning them to the unchanged candidate.",
      "evidence": "Import checks that the phase's candidate still equals head_sha, but a modified QA worktree is expressly 'Not a rejection reason.' A QA session can change an implementation defect, observe passing behavior in that altered worktree, and import a pass for the original defective commit. A dedicated disposable worktree protects the implementation from deletion but does not establish evidence integrity.",
      "recommendation": "Reject QA results when reviewed source differs from the packet candidate. Separate allowed generated outputs from source, verify source integrity, and require a fresh QA session after source mutation."
    },
    {
      "id": "ATLAS-102",
      "severity": "HIGH",
      "category": "approval-model",
      "file": "docs/workflow-state-machine.md",
      "location": "§3.1, G-CAND; docs/database-design.md §3, approvals lines 201–209",
      "description": "The protected-path approval required before candidate creation cannot be represented with the documented binding.",
      "evidence": "G-CAND requires an approval bound to the prospective tree SHA when diff guards do not pass. The approvals table has candidate_id and plan_id but no tree_sha or equivalent proposed-tree subject. The candidate does not exist until that guard permits its creation. An implementation must either block all such changes or invent a weaker binding outside the documented schema.",
      "recommendation": "Add an explicit immutable proposed-tree approval subject, including tree SHA and policy version, or create a non-deliverable candidate before approval and require approval of that exact candidate before testing or delivery."
    },
    {
      "id": "ATLAS-103",
      "severity": "HIGH",
      "category": "rebase-recovery",
      "file": "docs/recovery-strategy.md",
      "location": "§1, push reconciliation row; docs/github-integration.md §2, step 8",
      "description": "Push recovery contradicts the newly permitted rebase delivery path.",
      "evidence": "GitHub integration allows a rebased candidate to replace the previous remote revision using force-with-lease. Recovery permits retry only when the previous remote revision is an ancestor and explicitly says 'never force.' After a crash before a rebased push takes effect, the normal previous remote SHA is not an ancestor of the rebased candidate, so reconciliation blocks a legitimate operation instead of safely resuming it.",
      "recommendation": "Persist the push mode and expected remote SHA in the outbox intent. Reconcile rebased pushes separately and permit the exact recorded force-with-lease operation only while the remote still matches that expected SHA."
    },
    {
      "id": "ATLAS-104",
      "severity": "MEDIUM",
      "category": "rollback-correctness",
      "file": "docs/recovery-strategy.md",
      "location": "§6, final paragraph; docs/github-integration.md §2, step 12",
      "description": "The rollback command assumes a merge commit even though delivery always uses squash merge.",
      "evidence": "Delivery invokes gh pr merge --squash, producing a single-parent commit. Recovery prescribes git revert -m1 <merge_sha>; the mainline option applies to merge commits and fails for a normal squash commit. The documented revert phase therefore cannot implement its default rollback command.",
      "recommendation": "Use git revert <merge_sha> for squash commits, and select a mainline only after inspecting and validating a multi-parent commit."
    }
  ]
